hypothesis: A motif's effect on the lattice is predicted by boundary crossings per radial direction (not symmetry), and ume is the strongest keeper among the 11 mon
why: Crossings do NOT predict departure: r=+0.32, permutation p=0.38 (n=11, 3 independent sessions). tomoe has the HIGHEST crossings (2.29/ray, contradicting the 'tomoe~1 crossing' premise) yet ranks only 3rd; ume is 1.03 crossings, statistically identical to kikko's 1.00, yet the brief expected them 45pt apart. Deeper reason: fractal() applies abs(p) AND samples the mon as a REPEAT-tiled field, so the per-cell field is a tiled mosaic, not one centred motif - crossing counts measured on the centred silhouette do not survive that transform. Departure barely discriminates at all: common effect 76.1% with only 7.9pt between-motif spread (sd 2.85), i.e. ~96% of the effect is 'hexDist was replaced by a baked SDF' and ~4% is which motif. ume ranks 11/11 (LOWEST departure 71.76%) yet is visually among the better cells - so % departure is not a proxy for visual quality.

measured.method: lattice-nav REMOVED and paperCranes.seeds pinned; full-resolution 900x900 PNGs read with numpy/PIL (never canvas2D)
measured.luminance: ALL 11/11 BRIGHTEN at full res: base meanLum 9.35 -> 12.16..13.41 (+30.1% to +43.5%). No motif darkens.
measured.best_predictor: field RMS |beadDist-hexTerm| r=-0.682 p=0.013, but 6 predictors tested -> Bonferroni p~0.08, NOT significant

next: Stop using % pixel departure to rank motifs - it is saturated (76% common effect) and anticorrelates with visual quality. Rank by a structural/legibility metric instead.
